question: Should ClawHub adopt a first-class skill capability manifest, and which vocabulary, authority model, and advisory-to-required rollout should define the public trust contract?
rationale: Repository inspection confirms the missing capability baseline, but selecting the permanent public schema and deciding whether declarations are informational, verified, or enforceable changes a security-sensitive compatibility contract that automation cannot choose.

options.title: Advisory manifest first
options.body: Specify and expose declarations as unverified author metadata, report declared-versus-observed mismatches, and collect evidence before introducing submission requirements.

options.title: Retain inferred review
options.body: Continue using environment, install, and artifact analysis without adding a general author-declared capability baseline.

options.title: Require declarations immediately
options.body: Require new skill submissions to declare capabilities now, after defining validation and legacy-skill compatibility behavior.

recommendation.title: Advisory manifest first
recommendation.body: Specify and expose declarations as unverified author metadata, report declared-versus-observed mismatches, and collect evidence before introducing submission requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS and recent security-contract history make this the strongest available owner for the schema and trust-boundary decision.
